briefing.opening: Good morning. I will now begin the climate briefing for November 3, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and Global Warnings
sections.content: Today's reported climate news once again warns of the reality of the deepening global climate crisis. Glacier melt due to climate change is increasing flood risks, and the issue of corporate responsibility for this is being raised internationally [1, 11]. The European Union has revealed the specificity of the threat by disclosing climate risk information for 1,366 regions, including estimated damages from floods and heatwaves [12], and the intensity of heatwaves is also gradually worsening, with tropical regions becoming even hotter [16, 128]. These climate changes are having widespread impacts across society, such as reshaping Europe's flood maps and increasing home insurance premiums [131, 130]. Various parts of the world are encountering limitations in responding to the climate crisis, with the Welsh public sector, for instance, expected to struggle to meet its 2030 net-zero targets [124, 154]. In particular, the urgency of the climate crisis is further emphasized by the forecast that 2026 will be the warmest year on record [158], warnings of massive losses to mobile networks [152], and even the resilience of water, sanitation, and hygiene systems being put to the test [148].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Climate Change Response and Carbon Neutrality Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, multifaceted efforts to respond to the climate crisis are ongoing, demonstrating high civic awareness, particularly with 94% of Koreans supporting methane reduction and climate change concerns ranking first among 18 countries [3]. The Korea Climate Change Institute and The EAR Lab have signed an MOU to achieve carbon neutrality in the railway sector [2, 6, 39], and various organizations are collaborating, such as the Busan Port Authority and Korea Southern Power, which are jointly developing renewable energy to achieve carbon neutrality at Busan Port [26, 34, 41, 44]. Daegu City is encouraging citizens to practice carbon-neutral living through its 'Save Daefrica' campaign [17, 18, 19, 27], and community participation is active, with Gwangmyeong City being designated an environmental education city for the second consecutive time based on citizen-led educational achievements [23]. Furthermore, efforts in the agricultural sector to respond to climate change are noteworthy, such as Gyeongju City demonstrating new varieties of 'red beans,' an ingredient for Hwangnam-ppang, and Gyeongsangbuk-do supporting flower cultivation technologies [9, 13]. Incheon City is also accelerating its efforts to achieve its goal of becoming a leading carbon-neutral city by 2045, promoting a transition to green industries using climate tech [29, 40, 47, 59].

sections.title: 🌱 Expansion of Renewable Energy and Current Challenges
sections.content: With the imminent arrival of the 100 GW renewable energy era, the Korea Power Exchange is holding the 'Power Industry Advancement Forum' to discuss the challenges facing the power industry in this era [62, 71, 89, 101]. However, the supply of renewable energy is severely insufficient compared to the demand from companies [10], and many challenges remain, with the RE100 initiative urging the Korean government to expand renewable energy procurement pathways for businesses [86, 92, 93]. In particular, despite the 100 GW renewable energy target being close at hand, the investment budget for Grid Forming (GFM) to stabilize the power grid is noted to be very low [66], and there are strong calls for urgent innovation in grid operation, electricity markets, and regulatory frameworks [62, 71]. On a positive note, the Busan Port Authority and Korea Southern Power are collaborating on the joint development of renewable energy, including onshore wind and solar power, to achieve carbon neutrality at Busan Port [26, 34, 41, 44, 61, 63, 64, 65], and the importance of community-participatory renewable energy expansion and profit-sharing models is also growing [69, 72, 75, 78]. Furthermore, the search for technological solutions is active, with the advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) virtual power plant technology [98] and the emphasis on the importance of pumped-hydro storage for grid stabilization [84] being highlighted.

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Climate Change Awareness and Policy Discussions
sections.content: In the international community, awareness and policy discussions regarding climate change are being conducted in depth. Recent research has suggested the possibility that climate change may have actually prevented the onset of a new ice age [123], and it has been found that a majority of voters believe climate change threatens the 'American Dream' [126], indicating heightened social awareness. Brazil, the host country of COP30, established a significant turning point by announcing the world's first global roadmap for the phased elimination of fossil fuels [136, 156], and at COP31, to be held in Antalya, Türkiye, the implementation of climate targets previously promised by nations will be a major agenda item [135, 141, 146]. Alongside this, research into the complex impacts of climate change is active, including discussions that climate change could lead to a 'hidden hormonal crisis' beyond lung health [145], and the active role of policymakers is being emphasized, with suggestions that legislatures should seize the opportunity to address climate change and reduce energy costs [144]. However, the criticism that schools are failing to teach students about climate crisis action plans [151] leaves a task for the climate education of future generations.

briefing.closing: Through today's briefing, we have been able to confirm the severity of the climate crisis, as well as various domestic and international response efforts. Climate change is no longer a distant future problem; it is a reality directly connected to our daily lives, demanding urgent and sustained action. This concludes today's climate briefing.
